requirement:
Each `AgentConfig` variant carries the corresponding settings from
`trust_but_verify::agent`. Serde uses the `backend` field to select `bedrock`,
`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.

Choose [`BedrockConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.BedrockConfig),
[`OpenAiConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig), or
[`OllamaConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig) for the selected backend.
With settings omitted, OpenAI uses `gpt-6.1-sol`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`,
and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Ollama defaults to `http://localhost:11434`.

All three backend constructors start with an empty `options` map. Calling
`option(key, value)` inserts one inference setting. Calling it again with the
same key replaces its value and preserves the other settings. An `OptionValue` is
a `String`, `Boolean`, `Integer(i64)`, `Float(f64)`, `Array`, or `Map`. Arrays hold
option values and maps associate strings with option values. These serialize as
the corresponding untagged values. Backend calls reject nonfinite floats,
including those nested in an array or map.

`BedrockCredentials` contains `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`, both
`SecretString`, and an optional `session_token` of the same type. Construct a
`SecretString` from `String` or `&str`. `expose_secret()` borrows its value.
Serialization preserves the string, while `Debug` prints `<redacted>`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs` cover each obligation of `agent_config.settings`. I found one weak spot, covered below, and I do not count it as a gap.

- **Backend selection and flattened settings.** `mod[tests]/fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` deserializes `{"backend": ...}` objects for bedrock, openai and ollama. Each carries its settings in the same object. The test asserts that the serialized form equals the input and that a second round trip gives an equal config. `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` also checks that `{"backend":"openai"}` equals `AgentConfig::OpenAi(OpenAiConfig::new())`. `fn[configuration_debug_hides_credentials]` checks that an unknown field is rejected.
- **Defaults.**
  - `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` asserts the OpenAI model `gpt-6.1-sol` and the OpenAI endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1`. It also asserts the Ollama endpoint `http://localhost:11434`.
  - `fn[openai_uses_the_default_credential_variable]` runs a child process with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set. It shows that `OpenAiConfig::new().resolved_api_key()` reads that variable.
- **Empty options at construction.** `fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` serializes freshly built `BedrockConfig`, `OpenAiConfig` and `OllamaConfig` values. The output has no `options` key for any of them.
- **`option(key, value)` insert and replace.** In the same test, the Bedrock chain sets `a`=1, then `b`=true, then `a`=2. The result is `{"a":2,"b":true}`, so replacement works and the other setting is kept. The OpenAI and Ollama builders insert an option and the test checks it. `fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` also sets two OpenAI options and checks that both are kept.
- **`OptionValue` variants and untagged serialization.** The nested round trip in `fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` covers integer, float, boolean, string, array and map values. `fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` checks that `1` deserializes to `Integer(1)` and `1.0` to `Float(1.0)`.
- **Nonfinite floats.** The same test checks that `OptionValue::validate` rejects infinity nested in a map. It also checks that `options_json` rejects NaN nested in an array inside an `OllamaConfig`. `AgentConfig::options_json` calls `validate` for every backend, so this is shared code.
- **Credentials and `SecretString`.** `fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` checks `BedrockCredentials` with and without `session_token`, in both serialization and deserialization. `fn[configuration_debug_hides_credentials]` checks construction from `String` and `&str`, `expose_secret()`, `Debug` printing `<redacted>`, and serialization preserving the string.

**Weak spot, not counted as a gap.** Same-key replacement is exercised only on `BedrockConfig::option`. The OpenAI and Ollama `option` methods are separate, identical one-line `BTreeMap::insert` calls. The requirement states the same behavior for all three, so I treat the Bedrock test as representative. A weaker, more conservative reading would want replacement checked on each backend.

There is no `{fixme}` acknowledgment and none is needed.
